binders: Universally quantify real constants K = bulkModulus and rho = density; these are implicit Lean parameters.
Universally quantify a bundled system of type LocalDef001 K rho, containing real-valued functions p(x,t) and u(x,t).
Assume proofs of K > 0 and rho > 0.
In the second conclusion universally quantify x,t ∈ R.
Within the system condition, for each x,t existentially quantify real derivative values pt,px,ut,ux; these witnesses may depend on the system, K, rho, x and t.
Within the second conclusion, for each x,t existentially quantify real derivative values wt,wx; these witnesses may depend on the system, K, rho, x and t.
hypotheses: The system supplies p,u : R × R → R such that for every x,t ∈ R there exist pt,px,ut,ux ∈ R with: τ ↦ p(x,τ) has derivative pt at t; ξ ↦ p(ξ,t) has derivative px at x; τ ↦ u(x,τ) has derivative ut at t; ξ ↦ u(ξ,t) has derivative ux at x; pt + K ux = 0; and ut + rho⁻¹ px = 0.
conclusions: The specified number c = sqrt(K/rho) is strictly positive.
For w(x,t) = p(x,t) + rho c u(x,t), at every x,t ∈ R there exist wt,wx ∈ R such that τ ↦ w(x,τ) has derivative wt at t, ξ ↦ w(ξ,t) has derivative wx at x, and wt + c wx = 0.
mathematical_definitions: All arithmetic, order, norms and topology are those of the real numbers; the real metric is |x − y|.
The two arguments of each function are ordered as x first and t second. The coordinate derivatives hold the other argument fixed.
HasDerivAt f a y means the ordinary two-sided derivative of f at y exists and equals a; for real functions, lim as h tends to 0 through nonzero real h of (f(y+h) − f(y))/h equals a.
Real.sqrt r is the nonnegative square root of max(r,0). Here K/rho > 0, so c is the positive square root of K/rho.
LocalDef008 is the pointwise system p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + rho⁻¹ p_x = 0 together with existence of all four indicated partial derivatives.
LocalDef005 constructs exactly the function p + rho c u.
LocalDef004 is the real-valued specialization of LocalDef006, which requires time and spatial derivative witnesses satisfying q_t + c • q_x = 0. For real values, c • q_x = c q_x.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of positive real constants K and rho and every bundled pair of functions p,u : R × R → R whose first partial derivatives exist everywhere and satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + rho⁻¹ p_x = 0 everywhere, set c = sqrt(K/rho) and w(x,t) = p(x,t) + rho c u(x,t). Then c > 0, and at every real point (x,t) the time and spatial partial derivatives of w exist and satisfy w_t + c w_x = 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Both independent variables range over all of R, including negative t. No interval, spatial boundary, restricted region or one-sided derivative is specified.
K and rho are fixed real constants, not functions of x or t; both must be strictly positive for the implication to apply.
The system parameter restricts the functions to pairs satisfying the coupled equations with all four partial derivatives everywhere; the claim is not about arbitrary real-valued functions.
The bundled condition rho ≠ 0 is redundant under rho > 0. Totalized reciprocal at zero and truncated square root on negative inputs do not affect cases satisfying the hypotheses.

The positivity implication is vacuous for parameter choices failing K > 0 or rho > 0. For positive parameters the bundled assumptions admit, for example, constant p and u, so their mathematical content is not inherently empty.

Only coordinatewise first derivative existence is required. The statement does not explicitly require continuous partial derivatives, joint differentiability, higher derivatives or a C1 regularity class.
Derivative witnesses are quantified separately at each point. No continuous derivative fields or uniform regularity estimates are specified.
The theorem concerns an already supplied system; it does not assert existence or uniqueness of solutions for prescribed initial or boundary data.
The conclusion specifies only the plus combination p + rho c u and its positive-speed transport equation. It does not state a corresponding equation for p − rho c u.
No characteristic representation, explicit solution formula, second-order wave equation, boundary condition, initial condition, physical units or additional physical interpretation is encoded.
